title: The Role of Digital Platforms in Data Markets: How Platform-Shared Market Data Through Advanced Analytics Empower Firm Innovation
authors: Yubo Chen; Xuebin Cui; Aishen Li; Banggang Wu; Liu Yang
near_miss_reason: Synthetic difference-in-differences (synthdid, not an admitted estimator) is the only estimator applied to the staggered design: Table 3 column 2 (article Section 4.3) aggregates cohort-by-cohort synthetic DiD estimates with not-yet-treated controls across the monthly adoption cohorts of 2021. The remaining main-text columns use the single May 2021 cohort against never-treated retailers (synthetic DiD in Table 3 columns 1 and 4, Table 4 and Figure 2; a panel-difference regression with quadratic time trends in Table 3 column 3; a PSM-matched two-group regression in robustness), so no TWFE or admitted modern estimator of the staggered binary adoption (retailers adopt the advanced-analytics tool in monthly cohorts with a never-treated pool) is reported. The shipped data are synthetic.
eligible_reason: Retailers on Taobao adopt the advanced-analytics tool in monthly cohorts (January-December 2021) with a never-treated control pool, so a staggered binary adoption design exists in all_sample_data.csv. However, the main analysis (Table 3 col 1, Table 4, Figure 2) uses the single May 2021 cohort against never-treated controls and is estimated by synthetic DiD (synthdid); the only staggered estimate (Table 3 col 2, Robustness_Staggered.R) is a cohort-by-cohort synthetic DiD with not-yet-treated controls averaged across cohorts; Table 3 col 3 is a single-cohort panel-difference regression with quadratic trends; the PSM-DiD robustness (Robustness_PSM_DiD.do, xtreg with i.time_id on a matched single-cohort sample) is a two-group design with one adoption date; the spillover regressions use a continuous peer-adoption-rate regressor. No TWFE or modern DiD estimator of the staggered design is reported. The shipped data are synthetic.
design_notes: Code (R + Stata): Main_Estimation_SynthDiD.R (Table 3 cols 1 and 4, Table 4 subgroups), Robustness_Staggered.R (Table 3 col 2), Robustness_Panel_Difference.do (Table 3 col 3), Robustness_PSM_DiD.do, Dynamic_Treatment_Effects.R (Figure 2), Robustness_Spillover_Analysis.R (fixest feols log1p(pay_amt) ~ peer_adopt_rate(_lag) | id + ind:ds, cluster id ds), Produce_Figures.R, SynthDiD_Helper_Functions.R, prepare_publication_datasets.py (generates the synthetic data). Data: main_analysis_data.csv (1,882 retailers x 12 months of 2021: 554 treated cohort 20210531, 1,328 never-treated cohort 3, plus non-user cohort 9); all_sample_data.csv (126,720 rows, 12 monthly periods; unit cohorts: 0: 5,418, 3 (never treated): 1,332, 20210131 pioneer: 893, 20210531: 606, 20210630: 252, 20210731: 276, 20210831: 192, 20210930: 188, 20211031: 219, 20211130: 186, 20211231: 105); data_2019.csv. Treatment tr = 1 when ds >= cohort for adopters, 0 for cohort 3. Outcome log(pay_amt) sales revenue; also sku_cnt, category scope, new SKUs, price, advertising. Staggered SynthDiD: for each cohort g >= 20210500, treated = cohort g, controls = units with cohort > t_end (not-yet-treated), K_pre=3, L_post=2, synthdid_estimate per cohort, ATT averaged with n_treated weights.
estimators_reported: synthetic_did (synthdid, single cohort vs never-treated; Table 3 col 1, Table 4, Figure 2)
staggered_synthetic_did (cohort-by-cohort synthdid with not-yet-treated controls; Table 3 col 2)
panel_difference_with_trends (xtreg lnsale x post ctt ctt2 i.month, fe; Table 3 col 3)
psm_did_single_cohort (xtreg outcome tr i.time_id, fe; robustness)
main_or_robustness: staggered design appears only as robustness (Table 3 col 2, synthetic DiD)
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Monthly adoption cohorts Jan 2021 (pioneers) and May-Dec 2021 in the synthetic all_sample_data; main analysis uses the May 2021 cohort only. Cohort 0 (5,418 units) is undocumented in the README and is excluded by the scripts' cohort filters.
modern_estimators_named: synthetic_did (Arkhangelsky et al.; not in protocol list)
